caption: A bird lands on the edge of a car's side mirror, and its reflection appears in the glass and moves in step with it.

sa.check: A bird lands on the edge of a car's side mirror.
Its reflection appears in the glass.
The reflection moves in step with the bird.
The landing comes first and the reflection appears with it.

pc.expect: The reflection appears the moment the bird is in front of the mirror and moves at the same instant as the bird.
pc.fail: It lags; or appears before the bird arrives; or stays after the bird flies off.

pc.expect: There is one bird and one reflection, and the reflection stays in the glass.
pc.fail: A second bird appears; or the reflection steps out; or the bird vanishes.

pc.expect: The reflection is a mirror image of the bird.
pc.fail: It is a different bird; or not mirrored; or upside down.

pc.expect: The mirror is rigid: the reflection is undistorted.
pc.fail: It ripples; or warps; or bends.

pc.expect: The bird keeps its wings and shape.
pc.fail: A wing detaches; or the bird splits; or merges with the mirror.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The plumage and the car stay the same.
pc.fail: The plumage changes; or the car changes colour; or the mirror housing changes.

note: Self-driven animal: where it goes is not judged. Only the reflection's relation to it is.
